introduction: Connecticut weatherization helps income-eligible households improve home efficiency and address related health and safety issues. Local Community Action Agencies administer the work.
description: Connecticut weatherization helps income-eligible households improve home efficiency and address related health and safety issues. Local Community Action Agencies administer the wor

sections.who: The state lists income eligibility based on state median income. The local provider checks the household and property requirements and whether work is available.
sections.get: Weatherization is energy-efficiency work in the home, not a cash payment for the heating bill. The provider determines appropriate measures after assessment.
sections.docs:
• Household income and member information.
  • Property address, heating details and ownership or lease records.
  • For rentals, ask about owner consent and required property paperwork.
sections.apply:
1. Find the local provider

    Follow the Weatherization in Connecticut link on the DEEP weatherization page.

  2. Complete the intake

    Ask the Community Action Agency whether its heating-assistance intake also screens for weatherization and which documents to submit.

  3. Arrange the assessment

    Discuss access to the home, health or safety concerns and any owner permission needed before work.
sections.after: Ask about waiting times and renewal. DEEP says applications can be submitted at any time and must be renewed annually.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using DEEP weatherization overview. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.
